title: Probe Lab: Kernel, Scheduler, and KV-Cache Performance Notes
body:
Purpose and context

This doc captures the Probe Lab experimental notes for the serving runtime: focused efforts to surface regressions and understand interactions between kernel selection heuristics, request scheduler policies, and KV cache behavior. The goal is to build reproducible microbench probes that: 1) isolate perf regressions during releases, 2) exercise edge cases in scheduling and batching, and 3) stress KV cache semantics (prefix sharing, eviction, warm/cold transitions). This is an operational working log — not a final spec.

High-level hypotheses we are testing

- H1: Kernel selection changes that favor smaller GEMM kernels improve p50 but can regress p99 when sequence-length distributions are bimodal.
- H2: Scheduler timeout/backoff policies interact badly with caching: under high prefix reuse, aggressive batching can cause stalls when the KV cache warmup threshold is mis-sized.
- H3: Light-weight quantized kernels (4-bit) have lower throughput variance for short sequences but amplify tail latencies when KV cache lookups land on remote shards.

Measurement principles

1) Keep probes small and deterministic: each microbench targets one subsystem (kernel, scheduler, or KV) while mocking or pinning the rest.
2) Use trace-seeding to reproduce real-world arrival patterns (session affinity, prefix-ratio, user think-time).
3) Record: per-token latency histogram (log-buckets), CPU/GPU utilization, kernel bindings, scheduler decisions (why a request waited), and KV cache hit/miss events with timestamps.
4) Seed reproducible data into KV cache between runs (same key space and TTLs).
5) Use randomized seeds for microbench param sweeps but store them in artifacts for replay.

Harness architecture (probe-lab harness components)

- probe-client: lightweight load driver that can replay traces or generate synthetic arrival functions (poisson, bursty, uniform inter-arrival). Outputs raw request logs and annotated per-request ids.
- controller: orchestrates runs, pins model variants and kernel selection flags, toggles scheduler policy, provisions KV cache state (warm/cold), and collects metrics.
- observer: aggregates runtime traces (A/B kernel traces, KV events), and converts them to analysis artifacts (p50/p90/p99, heatmaps of kernel usage).
- artifact-store: stores seeds, trace files, and run results (S3/GCS).

Probe categories and test matrix

1) Kernel microbench (isolate kernels)
- microbench-kernel-smallseq: short sequences (1–32 tokens), single-threaded inference path. Parameters: batch sizes [1,4,8,16], quantization [fp16, int8, nf4]. Metrics: per-token latency, kernel invocation counts, GPU SM occupancy.
- microbench-kernel-longseq: long sequences (512–2048 tokens), focus on KV streaming and KV cache hits. Parameters: KV cache hit rate [0%, 25%, 75%, 100%]. Measure memmove overheads and KV deserialization times.

2) Scheduler microbench (isolate scheduler behavior)
- microbench-sched-latency-sensitive: low-latency SLO scenario; arrival patterns: steady vs burst. Policies: immediate dispatch, wait-up-to-5ms for batching, adaptive batching. Metrics: scheduler queue time distribution, batch sizes achieved, failed-SLO rate.
- microbench-sched-fairness: multi-tenant mix with heavy and light tenants; policy knobs: weight-based fairness, priority inversion mitigations. Metrics: tail fairness (p95/p99 per tenant), starvation events.

3) KV cache microbench (isolate KV semantics)
- microbench-kv-warmup: measure time-to-stable for cache with synthetic warmup traces. Track eviction churn at high working set sizes.
- microbench-kv-prefix-share: multiple requests share prefixes; measure prefix dedup ratio, write amplification, and cost per token when prefix is served from cache vs recomputed.

Trace seeding approach

- Real-trace sampling: sample 6 production traces (various apps) and sanitize them (no PII), convert to seed files with arrival times and prefixes.
- Synthetic trace generator: parameterizable to reproduce high variance, think times, prefix reuse. Use the same RNG seeds across kernel/scheduler matrix.

Observability fields to capture per-request (minimum)

- probe_id, request_id, arrival_ts, dispatch_ts, start_infer_ts, end_infer_ts, batch_id, batch_size, kernel_variant, kernel_time_ms, kv_lookup_time_ms, kv_hit_bool, cpu_mem_used_mb, gpu_util_pct, scheduler_decision (reason code).

Regression patterns we've observed (notes)

- Reg-2025-09-11: switching default GEMM micro-kernel to kernel-v3 decreased median for short sequences by ~12% but increased p99 by ~18% when mix contained a small number of long queries. Root cause: kernel-v3 better for small matmuls but caused longer warm-up for KV streaming path due to different buffer layout.
- Reg-2025-12-02: enabling adaptive-batching with default 10ms window caused queues to form under bursty workloads, increasing tail latency for low-priority tenants. Fix: add dynamic window shrink when measured queue depth > 100.
- Reg-2026-01-19: regression after PR #8421 where a scheduler fast-path bypassed KV cache warm-checks for cold keys; resulted in increased remote reads and p95 spikes. Patch reverted; follow-up change introduced explicit warm-check with asynchronous prefetch.

Triage playbook for a detected regression

1) Reproduce the regression locally via probe-client using the same seeds. If non-deterministic, run 10 iterations and collect traces.
2) Narrow to subsystem: flip kernel-selection flag; switch scheduler to naive immediate dispatch; force KV cache to 100% warm or 0% warm. If regression disappears after any flip, candidate subsystem found.
3) Capture kernel traces: annotate call stacks and buffer sizes to detect layout mismatches.
4) If KV-related, enable kv-verbose logs to fetch keys and latencies; map to remote-shard map.
5) Open JIRA with attachments: seed file, controller run config, aggregated histograms, and a short repro guide.

Example run command (probe-controller)

# run kernel smallseq fp16
probe-controller run --seed seeds/smallseq-bimodal.json --matrix kernel=kernel-v3,fp16 --policy=immediate --kv-warm=75 --out artifacts/run-2026-02-28

Interpreting results quickly

- If batch_size histogram is skewed left (mostly 1s) but we expected 8–16, check arrival jitter and scheduler backoff.
- If kernel_variant shows >1% cross-over to fallback kernels, inspect failure logs for unsupported shapes or OOMs.
- KV miss spikes correlated with longer dispatch-to-start gaps typically mean prefetch was skipped or invalidated TTLs are too short.

Open experiments and next steps

- EXP-2026-02: microprobe hybrid-kv (local hot cache + remote cold store): measure p99 impact when remote fetch latency is 3x baseline. Plan: run 50 repeats with varying remote latency profiles (10–250ms).
- EXP-2026-01: scheduler-aware kernel placement: test policy where scheduler hints preferred kernel on dispatch to reduce runtime kernel selection overhead.
- Improve artifact diffs: automatic visual diff for p99 heatmap between runs.

Notes to reviewers

- This doc intentionally mixes notes, commands, and triage heuristics. Please add missing probe variants you rely on, and flag anything that duplicates other playbooks (I tried to avoid overlap). For reproducibility, if you run any probe please upload the seeds and configs to the artifact-store path noted above.

Short todo list

- [ ] Add automated p99 heatmap diff to observer pipeline (Lina)
- [ ] Harden kv-prefetch async path and add unit test for warm-check (Ethan)

Appendix: common flags and meanings

- kernel=kernel-v2|kernel-v3: selects GEMM micro-kernel variant.
- policy=immediate|adaptive|wait-Nms: scheduler dispatch policy.
- kv-warm=0|25|75|100: percentage of keys seeded into the cache before run.
